data.title: Peter Schreiber: a medieval finger ring from Horná Mariková
data.excerpt: A stray find of a band-shaped finger ring of sheet bronze with engraved decoration comes from the hamlet of Hapovce in the cadastral area of Horná Mariková, where it was found around 1980. Analogies from the cemeteries at Čakajovce and Krásno place it between the end of the 10th and the first half of the 15th century.

children.text: In terms of typology the ring itself belongs among the so-called band-shaped rings. It is probably made of sheet bronze and carries a strong glossy patina on the surface (fig. 4). The ring is decorated on its widened upper part with engraved ornament (figs 1–3). The decoration consists of short lines. The upper part of the ring was probably partly open, with the ends of the sheet bent towards each other.

The dating of the find probably falls within the medieval period. At the cemetery at Čakajovce, Nitra district, similar forms of ring were found in graves which are dated from the end of the 10th to the beginning of the 11th century (Rejholcová 1995, 18, 71).

The second cemetery at which there are analogies to the ring is Krásno, Topoľčany district. The rings from the grave finds at Krásno are dated to the first half of the 12th to the second half of the 13th century. The latest ring there is dated by a coin in the grave to the 14th or even to the middle of the 15th century (Krupica 1978).

blocks.alt: Peter Schreiber: a find of a finger ring from Horná Mariková

children.text: On the basis of the cemeteries mentioned we can therefore date the find of the ring from Horná Mariková broadly to the period from the end of the 10th to the first half of the 15th century. Despite this fairly broad dating, the object represents a unique find within the whole of the Mariková valley. From the cadastral area of the village of Horná Mariková we as yet know of no archaeological finds that would attest occupation in precisely this period, which can be designated more precisely as the High to Late Middle Ages.
As regards written sources, the oldest surviving record shows that the key source for the history of the Mariková valley is the charter issued by King Charles Robert in 1321 (Šulavík 1991).
